newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas church burns, sixth this year.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas church burns, sixth this year.

text.p: The Fredona Missionary Baptist Church in West Helena was destroyed by fire Thursday morning, the sixth in the state to burn this year.

Fire department officials said the 45-year-old frame structure, located in the Arkansas delta 120 miles east of Little Rock, was burning out of control when firefighters arrived. It is the fifth church with a predominantly black congregation to burn this year.
More than 30 churches have been burned in the south within the past 18 months, authorities report.
Federal agents began collecting evidence from the rubble Thursday afternoon. Agents said it would be at least a week before specimens they gathered could be analysed for evidence of arson.
They refused to speculate about a possible connection between Thursday's fire and the earlier church fires in Arkansas, at least three of which investigators said were deliberately set.
"The fact that the majority of the Arkansas churches that have burned were African-American is the only pattern we have to work with, assuming it is a pattern," said FBI. agent Dan Wehr.
"I was raised in this church. I feel like I'm dying," said Creamle Taylor, a 60-year member of the congregation, as he surveyed the ruins of the church.
"We figure we can build it again," said James Richardson, 82. "I'm mighty old, but I'm going to try."
